scenes.headline: The Art of War in a minute
scenes.narration: One of the oldest books on strategy fits on a few pages. Here is what it says.

scenes.headline: A very old manual
scenes.narration: The Art of War is a Chinese text on strategy, traditionally credited to Sun Tzu and placed in ancient China, often around the fifth century BCE.

scenes.headline: Its main ideas
scenes.narration: Know your enemy and yourself, plan before you fight, stay flexible as circumstances shift, and gather good intelligence.
items: Know your enemy and know yourself

scenes.headline: Thirteen short chapters
scenes.narration: It has thirteen chapters, from Laying Plans in the first to the Use of Spies in the last.

scenes.headline: Beyond war
scenes.narration: Readers apply it to business, sport and negotiation, though it was written about armies.

scenes.headline: Read it in an hour
scenes.narration: It is short, and a public-domain translation is free to read.
